searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's; the Irsai Olivér search counted with Frittmann. Five were restricted to a body's own domain (frittmann.hu three times, winesofhungary.hu and bor.hu twice) and read as primary for that body's own facts. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.

What a search contradicted was set right with its source; a fact on one secondary source alone was cut or, where the record's teaching hangs on it, hedged as that source's account and left open; a serving temperature the house or the Parliament's page gives was preferred to the house style.

tested: The founding of 1982 and the mother who kept the farm after the father died: the house's own family and timeline pages (search on frittmann.hu), Magyar Bor's winery page and a trade magazine (János making wine from 1982) agree on 1982; kept, with the 1987 and 1998 of other accounts left out.

Cserszegi Fűszeres bred in 1960 at Cserszegtomaj from Irsai Olivér and a Traminer: Wikipedia (Roter Traminer), Wines of Hungary (Gewürztraminer) and a Hungarian food site (Savagnin Rose) agree on 1960 and the place; Traminer kept. Wines of Hungary gives the planting permit of 1982, added.

The glass (white blossom, pear, apple, white fleshed peach, fruit rather than spice, light body, medium acidity) and the spritzer: the house's own product page; kept. The page pours it at 11 degrees Celsius, so the serve moved.

The first Kékfrankos Rosé of 1999 and first bottled Irsai Olivér of 2000: the house's timeline; kept as its account. Its claim to be among the first to bottle the plain's grapes after 1989 is the house's alone, told as its taking to bottling them.

Winery of the Year 2015: a trade magazine and a Hungarian wine site agree; the 2007 wine house on the house's page; kept. Irsai Olivér bred 1930 (the Szentpéteri explanation's fact): Wines of Hungary and an academic paper agree.
changed: story: the grape was said to be among the first wines the house bottled, unsourced; now that Wines of Hungary dates its planting permit to 1982 and that, by the house's own account, it took to bottling the plain's grapes after 1989.
story: the claim that other Kunság houses followed it in bottling Irsai Olivér, the house's alone and a claim of a first, cut.
wine.serve: was 8 to 10 degrees Celsius; now 9 to 11, the house suggesting about 11, by its own product page; the spritzer kept, soda water cut as not in the house's words.
open: The founding of 1982 rests on the house's timeline and Magyar Bor; one business daily has the brothers' company from 1998 and a London merchant has the modern winery from 1987, so the year is the house's founding by its own account.
The stainless steel of the sister whites rests on the author's reading of the house's pages and was not tested again here.

tested: Néró bred at Eger in 1965 from Eger 2 (Villard Blanc) and Gárdonyi Géza: Wines of Hungary, a business weekly and an encyclopaedia (Eger 2 is Villard Blanc by DNA in 2016) agree; kept. Recognised in 1993: the Parliament's page and Wines of Hungary; kept.
The Csábori Kétsor vineyard on a chalky base, the category wins of the 2020 and 2021 Néró Rosé, three generations, the sand and chalky loess of Kiskőrös: the Parliament's pages; kept.
The couple of hours of skin contact and the siller's couple of days: the business weekly alone, a further search found no second source; the hours hedged, the days cut.

The father's planting in the early 2000s: the weekly's wording reads as the winery's establishment and Magyar Bor gives 2013; cut. The Cabernero rosé gold of 2021: Wines of Hungary's own article; added.
changed: story: Néró was said to be registered in 1993 as a hardy, early ripening variety that spread little; now first officially recognised in 1993 (the Parliament's page and Wines of Hungary), early ripening and disease resistant and made mostly as rosé and in blends (Wines of Hungary and the business weekly); spread little cut as a judgement with no source.
story: the father's planting of Néró in the early 2000s rested on one business weekly, whose wording reads as the winery's establishment; cut, the family's taking up of the grape left undated.
story: added the Cabernero rosé of 2020, gold at Le Mondial du Rosé in 2021, by Wines of Hungary's own article (primary).

wine.making, others, traps, table: the siller's about two days and the rosé's couple of hours rested on the business weekly alone; the siller now longer on its skins, the rosé's couple of hours hedged as the weekly's account, the table says a short time.
cards[1]: the card on the couple of hours of skin contact, one secondary source, replaced by the Csábori Kétsor vineyard on its chalky base (the Parliament's page).

sources: the British drinks club's article, no longer needed for any fact kept, replaced by Wines of Hungary's article on the district's rosés, the source of the Cabernero gold.

Founded stays empty: Magyar Bor's 2013 beside three generations of family history.

swaps.why: Not a swap of producer but the author's reading of the plan's word: the Kékfrankos Rosé holds the word Rosé, its grape is certain and the Parliament's selection names its 2019 a category winner, while the blend stands first among the others; the key stays gal-szigetcsep and plan.json needs no change unless the read together agent prefers the blend.

swaps.ruling: no swap made; the pick stands for the read together agent's ruling
swaps.why: The author asked for a ruling, not a swap. The Brut's grapes, method and protected name stay unsourced after my own search, and every field says so plainly; the house is a true thin pick of Izsák's sparkling country. If the read together agent wants a wine with a sourced cépage, a still wine of the estate under a protected name would be the move, with a new author's pass.

The plan's Cabernet Sauvignon Rosé gold of 2020 was not found on Wines of Hungary's own domain, and the Kékfrankos Rosé is the bottling sold at home under the Kunsági name; the author proposed no swap, and Lantos as a fifth Soltvadkert house is no better sourced.

codexTension: The region record's producers line has Szentpéteri arguing for the plain's reds with old vine Kadarka and Kékfrankos; no source read here bears that out, the house is known for Néró rosés and siller. Reported, not edited.
The region summary calls the Kunság the place where the louse cannot live in quartz sand; the Frittmann record says the louse does not thrive there, the gentler wording; reported, not edited.
